Record Q1 revenue of $783M framed as proof the multi-brand portfolio strategy (Celsius, Alani Nu, Rockstar) is working; portfolio ~20% of the US energy market, two $1B brands.
Alani Nu integration complete with the full ~$50M of targeted synergies captured - a major milestone simplifying the operating model.
Alani Nu pro forma growth ~60% reported (~85% clean scanner); CFO provided a detailed scanner-to-reported bridge (Cherry Bomb timing, DSD mix, Canada/non-US add-backs, ~$5M non-cash GAAP item).
Celsius brand grew only ~6% - analysts pressed on the moderation; management redirected to portfolio share gains and did not quantify cannibalization, innovation-timing or SKU-rationalization drags.
SKU optimization J-curve - reduction runs ahead of the ACV build; plays out over a couple of quarters; TDPs soften as total SKUs decline while space gains add holding power.
Q1 Celsius innovation deliberately focused on assortment prioritization; moving into a more active period - Electric Vibe LTO live, a summer Celsius LTO planned.
Alani Nu Lime Slush LTO became the brand's top-selling tracked-channel flavor (following Cherry Bomb) - proof the flavor-rotation model is durable and not hero-flavor dependent.
Celsius Fizz-Free emerging as a meaningful platform - broadly distributed but early in item-per-store; SKUs optimized at higher velocity while scaling ACV.
Rockstar in a 2026 stabilization year - SKU reconfiguration substantially complete, early signs of improved core-item velocities; integration on track for H1 2026 completion.
Operating leverage strong - adjusted EBITDA margin up ~370 bps to 24.9%, GAAP net income more than doubled to $110M; adjusted SG&A down to 26.4% from 31.8% in Q4.

Q1 gross margin ~48.3% (+~90 bps vs Q4) hit by discrete costs - severe Northeast winter weather freight/freeze protection, Rockstar inventory rebalancing freight, rising Midwest aluminum premium and LME.
Path back to low-50s gross margin reaffirmed but timing/sequencing conditional on sustained commodity costs; Q2 a side step, Q3/Q4 a stair step up, continuing into 2027.
Company fully locked on aluminum conversion with price locks on other ingredients/vitamins; extending coverage into 2027-2028.
Margin catalysts: second NC manufacturing line (back-half 2026 benefit, full 2027), vertical integration and direct sourcing (2027+), price pack architecture (initial H2 2026, more 2027-2028).
First quarter managing the portfolio under PepsiCo category captaincy - unlocking food service and non-reported channels; food service mix difficult to break out.
Reaffirmed CAGNY space gains (~17% Celsius, over 100% Alani Nu); resets to be largely finalized through May-June; retailers leaning into energy, cold space expanding rapidly.
International expansion: Celsius launched in Spain via Suntory, Portugal next; Dublin global HQ established; partnerships incl Aston Martin Aramco F1, Palm Tree Music Festival, 23XI Racing.
Capital allocation grounded in three priorities - invest behind brands/integration, maintain balance sheet strength, return capital; buyback continuing in Q2.
Tone confident, disciplined, execution-focused; entering peak summer selling season well positioned.

More color on the moderating Celsius brand growth - frame or quantify the impact of limited Q1 innovation vs last year, SKU rationalization, and assumed Alani Nu cannibalization, and how to think about Celsius growth for the rest of the year.

Emphasized the Fizz-Free opportunity (velocity and takeaway increasing in Q1) and that SKU optimization carries a timing sequence as slower items are removed; optimization plays out over a couple of quarters with reduction ahead of the ACV build; two Celsius LTOs in coming months (Electric Vibe now, another in summer); TDPs soften while space gains add holding power; did NOT quantify the drags as asked.
Alani Nu revenue bridge & Pepsi-system shipment quality
Was there a shipment benefit or inventory build in the quarter, or is the delta just the impact of promo and allowances as Alani Nu moves into the Pepsi system?

Increased orders referred to building ACV across Q1 - expanding SKUs per location and total locations - which drove scanner growth and internal GAAP numbers; explained DSD-to-direct mix nuances (Celsius had a smaller direct business at its move-in and took pricing in 2022); a ~$5M non-cash GAAP amortization item is in the Alani Nu bridge vs ~$1M/quarter for Celsius.
Shelf space gains: food service mix & Alani Nu realization timing
For Celsius, how much of the ~17% gain is food service vs tracked channels; for Alani Nu, how far along the over-100% gas-and-convenience space gains are and when more flows through tracked channels.

Energy one of the fastest-growing within LRB, retailers leaning in (over 60% of sales historically convenience impulse); retailers anticipate adding significant energy space, cold space expanding rapidly; Alani Nu space largely in place, resets finalized through May-June, almost fully done before summer; food service difficult to break out (sometimes zero-sum); first quarter managing the portfolio under PepsiCo captaincy unlocked food service and non-reported channels.
LTO strategy: new innovation vs recurring hero flavors
Given the success of LTOs like Cherry Bomb and Lime Slush, how does management balance new flavor innovation against bringing the same popular flavors back every year?

LTO strategy provides optionality in portfolio leveraging, forecasting and planning - enables surprise and delight (especially Alani Nu) and leverages seasonal trends; successful LTOs generate trial/feedback that can become permanent SKUs at mid-year resets or the new season; Cherry Bomb was the first LTO in the Pepsi system, then Lime Slush, now Electric Vibe, with a variety more in H2; portfolio holds a ~21% US share.
Gross margin path & aluminum cost sensitivity (12-18 month trajectory)
With Midwest premium and LME moving up, how to think about the margin trajectory if there is a resolution to the conflict and potential downside for aluminum, over the next ~18 months.

Q1 gross margin ~48.3% (+~90 bps vs Q4); discrete offsets - Northeast winter weather freight, Rockstar inventory rebalancing freight, rising LME/Midwest premium - the first two largely behind the company by Q2, aluminum premium more impactful in Q2 since it spiked in March; fully locked on aluminum conversion with price locks on other ingredients, extending coverage to 2027-2028; clear path back to low-50s but timing/sequencing conditional; second NC line in H2 (full benefit 2027), vertical integration/direct sourcing 2027+, price pack architecture 2027-2028; Q2 a side step, Q3/Q4 a stair step up.
Comparable-basis Celsius performance, cannibalization & sequential margin

On a comparable basis, how have well-set Celsius planogram locations performed; has Alani/Celsius cannibalization phased off or should the company be modeled as a portfolio; and does 'side step' mean Q2 flattish vs Q1 with Q3 margin above 50%?

Bullish on the Celsius portfolio's unique consumer segment; rational optimization of slower items driving consistency, optimized SKUs showing increased velocity alongside larger ACV gains; stressed consistent flavors/SKUs across retailers as a repeat-purchase driver; Fizz-Free a Q1 success; confirmed a sidestep in overall margin Q1 to Q2 with further enhancement opportunities Q3/Q4 toward the low-50% target; did not directly quantify comparable-basis planogram performance or confirm an above-50% Q3 margin.
